newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville Power lowers non-firm, off-peak prices.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville Power lowers non-firm, off-peak prices.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration lowered its prices for non-firm power on Monday, but raised prices for California border deliveries during peak demand hours, the federal agency said Friday.
BPA offered non-firm power during light load hours for deliveries in the Northwest and California border at $15.50-16.00 per Megawatt hour (MWh) for Monday, down from $16.00-18.00.
But the agency's raised its offer for non-firm power at the California border during heavy-load hours (0700-2200 PDT) on Monday to $21.50 per MWh from $20.25 for Friday.
Prices for firm heavy load block power were unchanged at $19.25 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $20.00 for Southwest.
BPA's block prices for firm off-peak power in the both Northwest and California border were also slightly lower at $15.50, compared with $16.00 for Friday pre-schedulings.
